topic.title: Reflectance confocal microscopy and line-field confocal optical coherence tomography in hair loss: A systematic review and a glossary of nomenclature
topic.abstract: Background: Reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM) and line-field confocal optical coherence tomography (LC-OCT) are emerging noninvasive imaging techniques in hair loss, potentially bridging the diagnostic gap between trichoscopy and histopathological examination. Objective: To systematically summarize RCM and LC-OCT features across cicatricial and noncicatricial alopecias. Methods: This systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines and was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251134481). MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to February 28, 2026. Eligible studies included original studies and case reports of RCM and/or LC-OCT in hair loss. Results: Forty-one studies encompassing 517 patients were included in the qualitative synthesis. Cicatricial alopecias showed higher pooled prevalence of dilated vessels, exocytosis, adnexal inflammatory infiltrates, and periadnexal sclerosis, whereas rimmed dermal papillae and hair shaft miniaturization predominated in noncicatricial forms. Evidence for treatment monitoring was limited but promising. A harmonized glossary linking RCM and LC-OCT features to trichoscopic and histopathological correlates was proposed. Limitations: This review is limited by the relatively low number of included studies and lack of standardized reporting of imaging features. Conclusion: RCM and LC-OCT are valuable adjunctive tools in hair loss diagnostics and may aid differentiation between cicatricial and noncicatricial forms.

MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to February 28, 2026.
Results: Forty-one studies encompassing 517 patients were included in the qualitative synthesis.

sections.label: 배경
sections.title: Introduction
sentences: Hair loss encompasses a heterogeneous spectrum of cicatricial and noncicatricial disorders associated with substantial clinical and psychosocial burden.
Accurate and early identification of the underlying cause is essential for appropriate management, as delayed diagnosis may lead to permanent hair loss.1
Over the past 2 decades, trichoscopy has become an integral component of the diagnostic evaluation of hair loss, complementing clinical assessment and histopathological examination.

sections.label: 연구 방법
sections.title: Materials and methods
sentences: MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to February 28, 2026, alongside forward and backward citation chaining in Web of Science.

Levels of evidence were assigned according to the Oxford 2011 classification.47 The certainty of evidence for each outcome of the subgroup analysis was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach.48 Results were synthesized narratively.
Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic (<25%, low; 25% to 50%, moderate; >50% to 75%, substantial; >75%, high).

Inflammatory infiltrates were additionally identified in the epidermis (11/20; 55%), dermis (14/33; 42%), and adnexal structures (12/34; 35%), whereas melanophages (5/19; 26%) and dilated vessels (3/19; 16%) were infrequent.9, 11, 29, 37 In AA incognita, follicles in telogen or catagen and telogen germinal units were identified in almost all evaluated cases.37 On LC-OCT, 2 morphologically distinct subtypes corresponding to trichoscopic yellow dots were characterized: hyper-reflective amorphous material filling the infundibulum down to the mid-dermis (bright yellow-whitish dots on trichoscopy) was observed in 63/85 cases (74%), whereas hyper-reflective material overlying a hyporeflective roundish area (yellow dots with a bright collarette) was identified in 44/96 cases (46%).

Additional findings included dermal fibrosis (18/35; 51%), bright material filling follicular ostia corresponding to trichoscopic yellow dots (17/35; 49%), epidermal inflammatory infiltrates (11/35; 31%), and periadnexal inflammatory infiltrates (10/30; 33%).11, 34, 35 No LC-OCT studies on AGA were identified.

Dystrophic follicular patterns (22/24; 92%), black dots (82/111; 74%), yellow dots corresponding to empty adnexal lumina filled with refractile material (78/111; 70%), hair shaft miniaturization (69/101; 68%), and abnormal hair shaft morphology (64/111; 58%) were also observed.

Dilated vessels, abnormal collagen bundles, hyperkeratotic and dilated infundibula, and spongiosis were also frequently observed.6, 28 On LC-OCT, interface changes (18/19; 95%), dermal sclerosis (18/19; 95%), absent dermal papilla rimming (14/15; 93%), and mucin deposits (15/17; 88%) were most frequent.30, 42 A continuous hyper-reflective junctional band with basal cell vacuolization was additionally reported in all cases in 1 series.

Follicular fusion on LC-OCT was reported exclusively in dissecting cellulitis, which additionally demonstrated confluent hyporeflective cavities with scattered hyper-reflective dots corresponding to pustules and abscesses, dense perifollicular inflammatory infiltrates, perifollicular fibrosis, and dermal sclerosis.42 In folliculitis decalvans (FD), dilated vessels (25/25; 100%), exocytosis (15/15; 100%), fibrosis (23/25; 92%), obscuration of dermal papillae (23/25; 92%), and hair tufts (30/39; 77%) predominated on RCM.25, 32, 33 Follicular pustules, a hallmark clinical and trichoscopic feature of FD, were identified on RCM as round-to-oval structures with a well-defined dark halo containing reflective amorphous material in 64% of cases (25/39).

sections.label: 고찰
sections.title: Discussion
sentences: CIA dots were detected more frequently with RCM than with trichoscopy, and RCM has been used to propose a pathogenetic sequence underlying their development.38 Persistent periadnexal inflammation identifies patients at a risk of permanent CIA.
In morphea, psoriasis, DLE, or tinea, imaging findings often parallel those on nonhair-bearing skin,50, 51 allowing cautious extrapolation of extra-scalp criteria.

LC-OCT additionally offers 3-dimensional reconstruction and real-time trichoscopic integration, whereas RCM requires the VivaScope 1500 for trichoscopic correlation, which is less practical for scalp imaging.

sections.label: 결론
sections.title: Conclusions
sentences: Neither modality replaces clinical examination, trichoscopy, or histopathology, yet each delivers entity-specific clues, including mucin deposition and basal cell vacuolization in DLE, follicular fusion in dissecting cellulitis, CIA-like dots in drug-induced follicular toxicity, and subclinical hair regrowth preceding the clinical response in AA treatment.

- Methods: This systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines and was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251134481).
- MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to February 28, 2026.
- Results: Forty-one studies encompassing 517 patients were included in the qualitative synthesis.

[상세 내용] (논문 전문 5개 섹션에서 발췌)

◆ 배경 — Introduction
  · Hair loss encompasses a heterogeneous spectrum of cicatricial and noncicatricial disorders associated with substantial clinical and psychosocial burden.
  · Accurate and early identification of the underlying cause is essential for appropriate management, as delayed diagnosis may lead to permanent hair loss.1
  · Over the past 2 decades, trichoscopy has become an integral component of the diagnostic evaluation of hair loss, complementing clinical assessment and histopathological examination.

◆ 연구 방법 — Materials and methods
  · MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to February 28, 2026, alongside forward and backward citation chaining in Web of Science.
  · Levels of evidence were assigned according to the Oxford 2011 classification.47 The certainty of evidence for each outcome of the subgroup analysis was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach.48 Results were synthesized narratively.
  · Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic (<25%, low; 25% to 50%, moderate; >50% to 75%, substantial; >75%, high).

  · Dilated vessels, abnormal collagen bundles, hyperkeratotic and dilated infundibula, and spongiosis were also frequently observed.6, 28 On LC-OCT, interface changes (18/19; 95%), dermal sclerosis (18/19; 95%), absent dermal papilla rimming (14/15; 93%), and mucin deposits (15/17; 88%) were most frequent.30, 42 A continuous hyper-reflective junctional band with basal cell vacuolization was additionally reported in all cases in 1 series.
  · Follicular fusion on LC-OCT was reported exclusively in dissecting cellulitis, which additionally demonstrated confluent hyporeflective cavities with scattered hyper-reflective dots corresponding to pustules and abscesses, dense perifollicular inflammatory infiltrates, perifollicular fibrosis, and dermal sclerosis.42 In folliculitis decalvans (FD), dilated vessels (25/25; 100%), exocytosis (15/15; 100%), fibrosis (23/25; 92%), obscuration of dermal papillae (23/25; 92%), and hair tufts (30/39; 77%) predominated on RCM.25, 32, 33 Follicular pustules, a hallmark clinical and trichoscopic feature of FD, were identified on RCM as round-to-oval structures with a well-defined dark halo containing reflective amorphous material in 64% of cases (25/39).

◆ 고찰 — Discussion
  · CIA dots were detected more frequently with RCM than with trichoscopy, and RCM has been used to propose a pathogenetic sequence underlying their development.38 Persistent periadnexal inflammation identifies patients at a risk of permanent CIA.
  · In morphea, psoriasis, DLE, or tinea, imaging findings often parallel those on nonhair-bearing skin,50, 51 allowing cautious extrapolation of extra-scalp criteria.
  · LC-OCT additionally offers 3-dimensional reconstruction and real-time trichoscopic integration, whereas RCM requires the VivaScope 1500 for trichoscopic correlation, which is less practical for scalp imaging.

◆ 결론 — Conclusions
  · Neither modality replaces clinical examination, trichoscopy, or histopathology, yet each delivers entity-specific clues, including mucin deposition and basal cell vacuolization in DLE, follicular fusion in dissecting cellulitis, CIA-like dots in drug-induced follicular toxicity, and subclinical hair regrowth preceding the clinical response in AA treatment.
